title: Successor step for bounded abelian henselian comparison
statement: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], i:Spec(A/I) → Spec A the quotient-induced map [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and n>0. Fix q≥0. Assume that restriction on H^q [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is bijective for every abelian etale sheaf F [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] on Spec A killed by n. Then for every such sheaf G restriction on H^(q+1) is bijective.

source.place: Tags 09ZE and 09ZI, finite Z/n coefficient successor step

proof.text: Efface a source class using bounded closed-subscheme effacement with the identity closed immersion. Naturality and bijectivity of identity pullback transfer the killing equation back to the source. For the monomorphism a:G to G-prime take its cokernel Q; cancel the epimorphism G-prime to Q to show that n kills Q.

Use the long-exact ladder on 0 to G to G-prime to Q to 0. For a source class x in the kernel of restriction, source effacement and exactness yield y in H^q(X,Q) with boundary x. The restricted boundary vanishes, so restriction of y is the image of z0 in H^q(Z,G-prime). Preceding-degree surjectivity lifts z0 to z; preceding-degree injectivity for Q implies that the image of z is y. Exactness then makes x zero.

Efface a closed-fibre class x0 in degree q+1, again with coefficients killed by n. Exactness yields y0 in H^q(Z,Q) with boundary x0. Preceding-degree surjectivity for Q lifts y0 to y; boundary naturality says that the boundary of y restricts to x0.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09ZE and 09ZI; C3 formalized the full successor-degree diagram chase and reduced bounded effacement to its constructible finite-module step.

mathlib_searches.query: Effacement of bounded abelian sheaves implies a successor-degree henselian cohomology comparison from comparison in the preceding degree
A natural map on sheaf cohomology is bijective in successor degree if it is bijective in the preceding degree for all coefficients and positive cohomology classes can be effaced on both sites
